prediction_ref.short_label: Agent-harness vendors ship gVisor+OS-sandbox+VM containment specs by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
The June 6 Flowise CVE-2026-40933 thread is the cleanest support yet for the containment thesis. The CVSS 9.9 flaw is an OS command injection in Flowise's Model Context Protocol stdio adapter where a one-click chatflow import triggers code execution with the Flowise process's own privileges - i.e., the tool command runs directly inside the host context with no confinement.
Obsidian Security argues the allowlist-and-flag-validation patch "treats the symptom rather than the cause" because the stdio transport exists to execute code, and recommends operators disable stdio in favor of Server-Sent Events - an argument that the enforcement point has to be the runtime that launches and confines the tool, not the string it was handed.
Coming a week after the Langroid text-to-SQL flaw, two CVSS-9-plus framework RCEs make self-hosted agent platforms a clearly active attack surface, exactly the pressure that forces agent-harness vendors toward the predicted sandboxed/VM containment posture.
